title: Global Estimation and Mapping of the Conservation Status of Tree Species Using Artificial Intelligence
summary: For 21,691 unassessed tree species, the authors estimated 22,889 of 58,429 species overall (39.1%) as possibly threatened, raising coverage to 52,191 species; results highlighted differences across taxa and regions. Fivefold cross-validation on assessed species: binary classifier accuracy 83.7% (87.1% for not threatened and 78.1% for possibly threatened); 100 Monte Carlo dropout predictions characterized uncertainty. This is predictive assessment, not expert-confirmed IUCN status; higher-confidence filtering yielded 90% accuracy for fewer cases.
ai_technology: A supervised fully connected neural network using species occurrence, range, biome, climate and human-footprint features predicted extinction-risk categories for species without IUCN assessments.
